extract:
꿈에 카메라를 가져올걸 was a South Korean shoegaze band formed in 2009. It started at Seoul National University and later signed with Oreum Entertainment, the company that also manages 9 and the Numbers. The name translates as "I Should Have Brought a Camera in My Dream," and fans shortened it to Kumca (꿈카). It comes from a dream in which the band wanted to record what it saw, went looking for a camera, and watched the dream fade before finding one. Melon describes them as a mixed-gender five-piece post-rock and shoegaze-pop band fronted by a woman. Namu Wiki lists the lineup as Park Yeon (vocals), Mijang (electric guitar), Lee Jae-hoon (acoustic guitar), Jang Seung-up (bass) and Lee Kyung-haeng (drums). Ki Kyung-seo played bass at the time of the 소실 EP.

Lee Jae-hoon got the band started. Before 2009 he had recorded a solo demo of "오후 세 시" ("3 PM"). He wasn't happy with it, so he suggested putting a new group together to record the song. Park Yeon said "오후 세 시" began as a modern rock song but changed a lot by the time they recorded it, as the band worked out a style that suited them. The next song, "비상구" ("Emergency Exit"), set the standard for their sound after that change. Notes from the period describe them as a guitar-pop-leaning five-piece modern rock band that changed members several times and, from early 2011, began openly adding post-rock elements. In October 2011 they were chosen as a monthly winner of Hello Rookie, the new-artist contest run by the EBS live music show Space Gonggam. One of the judges, critic Kim Hak-sun, noted that the vocals worked as an instrument in their own right.

Their debut EP, 소실 ("Disappearance"), first came out as a self-released digital EP on November 20, 2011, with four tracks: "비상구," "오후 세 시," "476-20" and "테러." Mirrorball Music released it on CD and to streaming services on April 18, 2012, adding two bonus tracks, "소실" and "냄새." In a Weiv interview, Park Yeon explained that it was meant to be a demo, but everyone put so much work into it that they decided to release it as a record before moving on to a full album. The lyrics of "476-20" are a list of Seoul neighborhoods such as Seogyo-dong, Hapjeong-dong and Sangsu-dong. The second EP, 슈슈 (ShuShu), came out on June 26, 2013, distributed by Ogam Entertainment and planned by Pago Music. It has three songs: "슈슈," "에너지드링크" and a track named after the band.

The band came up in Seoul's indie scene alongside other Korean shoegaze acts. Critic Shin Hyunjoon interviewed them for Weiv under the title "Nu gazing," and the 소실 liner notes include comments from Shin and the musician Danpyunsun. The ShuShu release notes quote Jowall (of Moim Byul) saying he could tell from their first show that they were built differently from typical shoegaze bands. In 2012 the English-language blog Strange Seasons praised the way they wove the theme of dreams through all six songs. Their songs still turn up in shoegaze playlists. On Last.fm the band has about 5,000 listeners and 58,000 scrobbles.

After a long break, Kumca appeared on Oreum Entertainment's second compilation in 2016. It was their first new song in three years, "일상의 환상 (feat. Drain)." Around then they also announced that lead vocalist Park Yeon would be away from the band for a while. Namu Wiki says personal circumstances have made it hard for the members to keep playing, and that the band has effectively broken up. Mijang also plays guitar in the post-rock band Hail (해일). The band never made the full-length album its two EPs seemed to be leading up to.
title: 꿈에 카메라를 가져올걸
